title: Thirteen-bar truss with an overhang: joint deflection

source.work: Bentley Systems, STAAD.Pro Help, Verification Examples (public documentation, docs.bentley.com)
source.edition: STAAD.Pro Help v21 build (pages refer to the STAAD.Pro 2023 sample files), read 2026-11-22
source.notes: problem statement taken from the vendor page (text and input listing). The page cites: McCormac, Structural Analysis, 3rd ed. 1975, p. 271, example 18-2 - NOT opened for this project; no number is taken from it. The page's 'theory' values are recorded as printed; the program's own results are not used.

analysis: Plane truss (X-Y plane, Y vertical; uz of every joint held), joints and bars as in the page's input listing: bottom chord joints 1 to 5 at 15 ft spacing, upper joints 6 (15, 7.5 ft), 7 (30, 15 ft), 8 (45, 7.5 ft); bars 2-6, 3-4, 4-8, 4-5 with A = 1 in^2; 1-2, 2-3 with 2 in^2; 3-6, 3-8 with 1.5 in^2; 3-7, 1-6, 5-8 with 3 in^2; 6-7, 7-8 with 4 in^2; E = 30,000 ksi; joint 1 pinned, joint 3 on a roller (vertical support); 20 kip downward at joints 2, 4 and 5. Target of the page: the vertical deflection of joint 5. Units kip, in. Reference values: computed here from this statement (verification/derive/vendor_reference.py); the textbook cited by the vendor page was not opened and no number is taken from it.
